links.reason: In Kuruntokai 320 the drying catch (கொண்மீன் உணங்கல் ... இறவின் வாடலொடு) only describes the துறைவன்'s shore; it is not the place of any meeting, and the denial (நக்கதோர் பழியு மிலமே) is about the town's gossip. Kainnilai 54's heroine guarding prawns (இறவுணங்கல் யாம்கடிந்து) was deceived (பொய்த்து ... நலனுண்ட). Two different heroines in different situations are not incompatible claims about one thing; the link is a shared shore detail dressed up as a tension.

The contrast is real: யாமே ... கேண்மை அம்பல் ஆகற்க எனவேட்டேமே (the girls pray the bond not become gossip) against உறாஅதோ ஊரறிந்த கெளவை (the man welcomes it). But these are different speakers in different situations, not incompatible claims about the same thing, so TENSION overstates; the gendered reading in teaches is fair but generalises from two verses.

Natrinai 335 lists the sea whose sound never stops (பாடு ஓவாதே ... ஓதமும் பெயரும்) among the night's torments; Ainthinai Ezhupathu 60 makes the sea sleepless like her (எம்போல் ... துஞ்சாதது) and gives it her cause (அணிநலம் உண்டகன்றான்). The turn from tormentor to fellow sufferer is specific and accurate to both Tamil texts.

Lines 3-4 (இறந்து செயின அல்லது அரும் பொருட் கூட்டம் இருந்தோர்க்கு இல்) really do restate the Kural's maxim, and வினை இடை விலங்கல போலும் shows the planned work held back by her beauty. But the Natrinai does not dispute the maxim; it shows a motive overriding it, so 'marks the limit of the Kural's rule' overstates what is a check on action, not on the claim.

தெரிவிலர் தீங்குழல் ஊதும் பொழுது does make the herders unaware, which adds to the Kural's kill-weapon flute (கொல்லும் படை) the point that no one aims it. But lines 1-2 are lost and line 4 breaks off at அரித, so what the fragment says about the hour cannot be checked, and the link rests on one surviving line.
links.text_issue: Lines 1-2 are lacunose and line 4 breaks off (அரித); the sense is a reconstruction.

links.reason: Both are Idaikkadanar's homecoming speeches to the charioteer, a point the note misses. Teaches depends on reading விருந்தெதிர் கொள in Akananuru 374 as the wife receiving the husband as guest; it can as well mean she will now receive guests, which a wife does only with her husband home, and then the two poems agree with Natrinai 221's விருந்து விருப்புறூஉம் rather than placing the hero differently.

The verbal echo is real: இல்லெலி in Kuruntokai 107 and இல்எலி வல்சி in Akananuru 122, and the cock ends the night in both (மனைச்செறி கோழி; கணங்கொள் சேவல்). But the rat-hunter in Akananuru 122 is the owl (கூகை), while the curse in Kuruntokai 107 sends the cock to the wildcat (வெருகு), so 'the very rat-hunters of the courtship poem' is false, and 'marriage did not free the lovers' night' is an overreading.

Both are Paranar's and both use Nannan as an exemplum: Kuruntokai 73's Kosar (நறுமா கொன்று நாட்டிற் போக்கிய) as a model of hard scheming, and Kuruntokai 292's பெண்கொலை புரிந்த நன்னன் as a curse. But Kuruntokai 292 says only புனல்தரு பசுங்காய், not that the fruit came from Nannan's mango, and neither poem gives an order of events, so 'both halves of one tale' comes from tradition, not the Tamil. Whom the Kosar drove out (போக்கிய) is also not fixed by the line.

Both pair the town's talk with the mother: ஊரார் பெண்டென மொழிய ... அன்னை in the Ainkurunuru, ஊரவர் கெளவை ... அன்னைசொல் in the Kural. But வெம்மை can be plain 'heat' as well as fever, and teaches' claim that the couplet's metaphor 'began as the lover's cover story' asserts a derivation neither text shows.

The slipping bangle and wasted shoulders (ஒண்டொடி நெகிழச் சாஅய் மென் தோள் பசப்பது; பைந்தொடி சோரும் ... தோள்) are the commonest sign in akam, so the shared image is generic. The difference in use, evidence in a disclosure to அன்னாய் against the Kural's bare portrait, is accurate, though line 1's conditional (உண்துறை அணங்கிவள் உறைநோய் ஆயின்) is uncertain.

Kuruntokai 153's heart that once feared the owl and monkey (அஞ்சுமன்) now travels the night slope (சாரல் நீளிடைச் செலவா னாதே), and Kuruntokai 141 asks him not to come at midnight (ஆரிரு ணடுநாள் வருதி ... வாரலோ). These are different poets' heroines, though. Kuruntokai 141's plea is also a turn toward meeting by day (the mother's errand to the millet field), so 'care for him rather than prudence she lives by' is a motive neither poem states.

Both heroines address the crab (கொடுந்தாள் அலவ; அலவ), one to spare the chariot track (நடந்து சிதையாதி) and the other to carry her word (சொல்லல் வேண்டுமால்). That is a distinctive shared address. But the reason teaches gives, that the crab 'alone moves where the lover moved', is not in Akananuru 170, which chooses it because grove, backwater and punnai will not speak. The link is better typed as same_image.

The divine comparison is shared (வரையர மகளிரின்; அணங்குகொல்), but the link turns on reading அரியள் as 'hard to win'. It can equally be 'rarer', a measure of beauty. Ainkurunuru 191 also ends with her carrying off his heart (கொண்டொளித் தோளே), not with despair, so 'measures distance as often as beauty' is unsupported, and nothing in either verse limits the other.

Both set the rains begun (கார்தொடங் கின்றே, in both) against the man in a king's camp (வெற்றி வேந்தன் பாசறை; வெஞ்சின வேந்தன் வியன்பெரும் பாசறை). The friend's assurance (அமைகுவர் அல்லர்) and the heroine's despair (நம்மும் உள்ளார்) are the standard split between the வற்புறுத்தல் and பருவங்கண்டு அழிதல் situations: different speakers, not incompatible claims. The teaches is true but restates that convention.

The shared image is specific and meaningful: the bee and the fragrance of her hair (கூந்தலின் நறியவும் உளவோ; வண்டினம் மொய்ப்ப ... கூந்தல் நாறும்நின் மார்பே). Kuruntokai 2's bee is asked a question rather than witnessing a boast, so 'witnesses against him' is a little embroidered. The link is better typed as same_image than DEVELOPS.

The echo இவ்வூர் ... பிறதொன் றாகக் கூறும் / இகந்துறைவர் ஏதிலர் என்னும் இவ் வூர் is close, and the contrast between inner certainty and the appeal to fate (ஆங்கும் ஆக்குமோ வாழிய பாலே) is accurate. But 'a demand for marriage' overstates a wish addressed to fate, and the marker flagged line 5 as uncertain.

Both play on ஒருநாள: ஒருநாள் ... தவப்பன் னாள் against ஒருநாள் எழுநாள்போல். But the Kural stretches one day of waiting, while Kuruntokai 271 sets one day of union against many days of wasting. These are different claims sharing a number figure, so QUALIFIES does not fit, and the link amounts to a shared figure.

The parallel is real and specific: the monkey that cannot survive widowhood (கைம்மை உய்யாக் காமர் மந்தி ... பாய்ந்துயிர் செகுக்கும்) and the queen for whom pond and pyre are one. But teaches says the akam friend 'borrows' the queen's refusal, a derivation nothing in either poem supports, so this is a cross-domain parallel rather than development.

Both are marutham buffalo-in-the-pond scenes addressed to the bard (மதஎருமை தண்கயம் பாயும் ... பாண; எருமை பழனம் படிந்து ... உரைபாண). But Ainthinai Ezhupathu 49 does not 'tell the bard to deliver the buffalo as the man's portrait': it tells him to speak to the women (பெண்டிர்க்கு உரை), and the buffalo stays in the town's description. Teaches uses one inferred reading to prove another.

The shared phrase is exact, மலர்தலை உலகம், and the claims really pull against each other. Purananuru 24 closes with those who did not pass with the many but stayed in fame (பலர்செலச் செல்லாது நின்று விளிந்தோரே), while Maduraikkanchi 235-237 counts kings who ruled with fame spreading (உரைசெல) as more than the sand (திரையிடு மணலினும் பலரே) and gone (கழிந்தோரே). The same-poet claim rests on the colophons (Mangudi Kizhar, with Mangudi Maruthanar as a variant).

The link needs ஒத்தன்று to mean 'did not match'. In this idiom -அன்று is the past neuter ending (as வந்தன்றே in Ainkurunuru 342, நின்றன்று in Natrinai 335), so பொழுதிற்கு ஒத்தன்று is more naturally 'the bard's lute was in tune with that joyful hour'. On that reading the lute accompanies the family scene rather than losing to it, and the Kural's comparison (குழல் இனிது யாழ்இனிது என்பதம் ...) has no scene behind it here.

Ainkurunuru 342 is spring (இளவேனிற் பத்து: the nunavam in scent, சுரும்புகளித்து), while Kar Narpathu 4 is the rains (கடுக்கை, peacocks), so 'the same flowering' is false. Ainkurunuru 342 also does not call the season a sickness (அவரோ வாரார் தான்வந் தன்றே). The pairing rests on the stock 'season comes, he does not' situation.

Both describe enemy kings submitting (பணிந்துவழி மொழிதல் அல்லது; வேற்று அரசு பணி தொடங்கு), and Purananuru 17 does quote the enemies' reasoning (இழந்து வைகுதும் ... உடன்று நோக்கினன்). But submission to the king is the shared puram topic. The fragment's colophon names no king, and nothing shows its boast 'rests on' the scene in Purananuru 17, which adds detail rather than limiting it.

Kalittokai 11 has the man himself report beasts' care on the cruel road: the tusker lets its mate drink the scant muddy water first (சின் நீரைப் பிடி ஊட்டிப் பின் உண்ணும் களிறு), and the stag shades the doe. Aimpathu 38 puts the same scant water (சிறுநீரை எய்தாதென்று) and a stag's feigned drinking (கள்ளத்தின் ஊச்சும்) on the road his heart took (உள்ளம் படர்ந்த நெறி), offering it as the same proof. The added pretence is a real refinement; the speaker of Aimpathu 38 is not certain.

The adjacent verses do meet: the wife who dreads guests brings no good (விருந்தஞ்சும் ஈர்வளையை) and the chaste wife is a friend by tending guests (நல்விருந் தோம்பலின் நட்டாளாம்). But verse 64 lists three equal debts (இம்மூன்றும் ... கடன்), so 'hospitality is the wife's first duty' and 'failing it alone' are not in the Tamil.

Both friends call the rain untimely (வம்ப மாரி; வம்புப் பெய்யுமால் மழையே). Kuruntokai 66 discounts the sign by calling the konrai foolish (மடவ மன்ற), while Kuruntokai 382 proves the rain false from his absence (பருவம் ஆயின் வாரா ரோ). The shift to making his coming the test of the season is real. 'From blaming the tree to denying the season' slightly overstates it, since Kuruntokai 66 also denies the season.

Paripadal 9 has like outdo like (ஆடல் நவின்றோர் அவர் போர் செறுப்பவும் ... வல்லாரை வல்லார் செறுப்பவும்), and Paripadal 17 sets each human sound against a thing of the hill (ஒருதிறம் ... யாழ் / வண்டு; விறலியர் / பூங் கொடி) in a contest (மாறு எதிர் கோடல்). Teaches is specific and true, but song 17 widens song 9's figure rather than limiting it, so the type should be develops.

Both are veri-rite poems that deny the god's agency. Akananuru 388 asks whether the velan's god hunts with a bloodied arrow (ஊன்புரள் அம்பொடு ... வேட்டம் செல்லுமோ நும்மிறை), giving the god the lover's emblem. Ainkurunuru 250 names the god by his own peacock and valli (மடமயில் ஆலும் ... வள்ளியம் கானம் கிழவோன்) to deny him. So 'in each other's emblems' holds for only one of the two, and the rest is the shared veri topic.

The tiger-and-elephant figure is shared (குஞ்சரக் கும்பத்துப் பாய்வன ... வேங்கை இரும்புலி போன்ற; யானை வெரூஉம் புலிதாக் குறின்). But ஊக்கம் is only the Kural chapter's title and is not in verse 599, so 'the Kural's own word' is false, and the claim that drive overcomes size is the chapter's moral, not the couplet's.
links.text_issue: The packet's Kural 599 text has encoding junk (஦வ்ருஉம்) for வெரூஉம்.

links.reason: The shared diction is real and close: வேறுபுலத்(து) இறுத்த ... தானையொடு / வேறுபுலத்து இறுக்கும் தானையோடு, மைந்துமலி / மைந்து மலிந்த, and வந்தனென் ... கண்டனென் / வந்து இனிது காண்டிசின். That supports a set scene. But Purananuru 22 is also a war camp (வியன் பாசறை, தும்பை, வெறிக் குரவை) of a king still leading his army into enemy land, so 'settled order against war still pending' overreads கந்து சேர்பு நிலைஇ against கந்துகால் கீழ்ந்து.

Thirumurugatruppadai 167's நால்வேறு இயற்கைப் பதினொரு மூவர் is exactly spelled out in Paripadal 8: பதின்மரும் இருவரும் (12), மருந்து உரை இருவரும் (2), திருந்து நூல் எண்மரும் (8), and ஆதிரை முதல்வனின் கிளந்த நாதர் பன்னொருவரும் (11), four groups making 33. In both the gods come to Murugan (வந்துடன் காண; பற்றாகின்று, நின் காரணமாக). This is specific and correct.

The distinctive image is shared: the fallen vengai flowers look like a tiger (வேங்கை ஒள்வீப் புலிப்பொறி கடுப்ப; இளவேங்கை கான்றபூ ... வயவேங்கை ஏய்க்கும்). Both are friends' arguments against the night visit, one through the frightened she-elephant (இரும்பிடி இரியும்) and the other through the girl (வாழாள்). Teaches' point that the case rests on a likeness, not a real tiger, follows from the Tamil.

This is a genuine conflict on the same case, gladness in the giver. Perunchithiranar will take even a kunri seed's worth if it is given gladly (உவந்து நீ இன்புற விடுதி யாயின் சிறிது குன்றியும் கொள்வல்), while the Kural holds that not asking even from those who give gladly is worth a crore times more (கரவாது உவந்தீயும் ... இரவாமை கோடி உறும்). The shared உவந்து sharpens it.

நகல் in Kural 860 is friendliness set against இகல், and நகுதல் in Kural 784 is laughter between friends. These are two senses of one root, and neither verse limits the other. Teaches says only that the root is valued differently, which is a shared word, not a link.

The pair turns on the same verb: மறந்தோர் மன்ற மறவா நாமே against மறப்பின் எவனாவன் ... மறப்பறியேன். In the Kural not forgetting is her own bind (உள்ளினும் உள்ளம் சுடும்), while Avvaiyar turns it into a charge against the man, backed by the seasonal rain he promised to precede (கால மாரி ... முன்வரல் ஏமம் செய்தகன் றோரே). The contrast is specific and accurate.

The rare figure மெல்லியான் பருவம் is in both poems of the same poet (colophon நல்லாந்துவனார்). In 129 the dark comes like the weak reign after a just king (அரசன் பின் ... மெல்லியான் பருவம் போல் மயங்கு இருள் தலை வர); in 120 the evening vanishes as the enemy of a weak reign is driven off when a good king appears (நல் இறை தோன்றக் கெட்டாங்கு). Teaches, that the lover's return stands in for the king's, is exact.

Akananuru 78 names Paari with Kapilar (வாய்மொழிக் கபிலன் சூழ), holding out for years (யாண்டுபல கழிய) and driving off the kings (வேந்தர் ஓட்டிய). It uses the fragrance of his pool (தீம்பெரும் பைஞ்சுனைப் பூத்த தேம்கமழ் புதுமலர்) for the girl's brow, which the note says. Purananuru 109 also praises Parambu's pools (மீன் கண் அற்று அதன் சுனையே), a shared image the note does not cite but which makes SAME_IMAGE fit.

Kuruntokai 140 asks how the noisy town knew the grief she bore in silence (தாங்கிய எவ்வம் யாங்கறிந் தன்றிவ் வழுங்க லூரே), and Kural 1180 answers that the secret is not hard to learn for those whose eyes beat it like a drum (அறைபறை கண்ணார்). The question-and-answer fit is specific and true to both.

The fit is neat: பிரிந்தென ... ஒண்ணுதல் பசப்பது names the leaving with the pallor, which is exactly what Kural 1188 says no one does (துறந்தார் அவர்என்பார் இல்). But the speaker in Kapilar's அன்னாய்ப் பத்து is not fixed, so 'the friend as the one voice' leans on the marker's attribution and overstates.

Naladiyar 370 says the fresh flood ends with the rain (புதுப்புனலும் மாரி அறவே அறுமே) as a figure for courtesans' love. Paripadal 7 prays that the bathing never be left (நின் படிந்து நீங்காமை), a wish about the bathers made at a yearly festival. The two claims do not conflict, and nothing shows the didactic poet 'reversing' the hymn. The link rests on a shared word, புனல்.
links.text_issue: Line 85 has a lacuna; line 81 was repaired from another site.

links.reason: On the plain reading the two value the same pallor in opposite ways. The Kural accepts it if he fares well (பசக்கமன் ... நயப்பித்தார் நன்னிலையர் ஆவர் எனின்), while Velliveethiyar counts her beauty as spilt milk, useful neither to her nor to him (எனக்கு மாகாது என்னைக்கு முதவாது பசலை உணீஇயர்). The sacrifice-or-waste contrast is specific.

Same poet (Peri Saathanar), with a formula clearly shared: நம்மொடு ... கிளி கடிந்து / கிள்ளை நம்மொடு கடிந்தோன். In Natrinai 25 the friend pleads the silent visitor's case (சொல்லிடம் பெறாஅன் பெயர்ந்தனன்), and in Akananuru 242 the mother does not know this same man came in love (பண்புதர வந்தமை அறியாள்) and calls the ignorant velan (அறியா வேலன்). The point about the friend's knowledge against the mother's ignorance holds; 'a single courtship' means a conventional sequence, not one story.

The man as sun is shared (ஞாயி றனையன்; வெஞ்சுடர் அன்னானை), but it is a stock comparison. 'Dependence' rests on the nerunji turning after the sun, which Kuruntokai 315 does not say (நெருஞ்சி யனையவென் ... தோளே). Thinaimalai 89's sun-and-moon pair (தண்சுடர் அன்னாளை) is the travellers' description of a matched couple, not a statement about parity.

iraicchi.act: the reed gives itself as a float to every woman bathing in the flood (புனலாடு மகளிர்க்குப் புணர்துணை உதவும்)
iraicchi.sense: the man of that town likewise makes himself partner to all the women of the town, so he is no longer 'ours' (ஊரன் ஆயினும் ஊரனல் லன்னே).

poems.note: The reed could be read as a scene mapped part by part, but it is one carrier doing one act, and the poem states only that he is 'not ours', not the infidelity itself.
The crow stirring the cold backwater at midnight may hint at the town's prying, but no one-sentence implication for the lovers can be fixed.

iraicchi.act: the jasmine creeper embraces the kurundham in the rains (குருந்து அணைய)
iraicchi.sense: in the season even the creeper is joined to its tree while she is left alone, so how can she bear it.

poems.note: Reading குருந்தனைய as குருந்து அணைய (embracing the kurundham) rather than 'like the kurundham' decides the tag.

iraicchi.act: the old lame heron brings sea fish to its pregnant mate who stays in the field and cannot go to the grove
iraicchi.sense: the bird provides for its mate as the hero should provide for the girl by marrying her, and seeing it makes her weep.

poems.note: The cloud and the peacock answering it are the stated object of her distress (ஏதில கலந்த இரண்டற்கு), so striking them removes the poem's sense.
The koel 'lied' (பொய்த்த குயில்) is the poem's main statement, so the carrier cannot be struck.
The ripening millet and the parrots are the literal setting of her task, so they yield at most one correspondence (ripened crop to a girl come of age).
Tusker as the hero is the only clear correspondence; the tiger and the kin have no fixed partners in the love situation.

iraicchi.act: the mated anril pair, having fed in the backwater, roost together on the palmyra
iraicchi.sense: the birds keep together after feeding while the lord who took her beauty has left her, so she asks them to demand it back.

iraicchi.act: the heron sleeps in the sweet shade of the punnai
iraicchi.sense: the bird sleeps at ease while her eyes, since the lord left, cannot sleep (பாடொல் லாவே).

poems.note: The hunter coming home to his hut with his kill may set a settled household against the night visits, but the poem's own point is the day visit, and no single implication is fixed.

The tiger that has sheltered its newly delivered mate and hunts for her is the textbook kind of carrier, but here it serves as the danger on his path, and its care does not clearly imply anything for the lovers.

ullurai.anchor: என் நோக்கினளே அன்னை; thurai செறிப்பு அறிவுறுப்பான்

poems.note: The sand doll the girls made, with njaazhal flowers spread on its breasts like sunangu, stands for the girl herself come of age; that is why the mother watches her and confinement is due. The -இன் of சுணங்கின் joins the flowers to the doll, not to the girl.
The subject that leaps into the pond is not named in the surviving text, so no single carrier can be fixed.
The colophon files Nedunalvaadai as வாகை (கூதிர்ப்பாசறை), a puram poem, so both fields are null by the rule.
The hornbill fleeing the rustling leaves is set against the hero's ease with his companion, a contrast of mood rather than an act a lover does.
